title: Comprehensive Characterization of the Coding and Non-Coding Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms in the Tumor Protein p63 (TP63) Gene Using In Silico Tools.
authors: Akter, Shamima; Hossain, Shafaat; Ali, Md Ackas; Hosen, Md Ismail; Shekhar, Hossain Uddin
one_liner_zh: 该研究用计算工具和MD模拟表征TP63基因SNP对蛋白稳定性及TP63-DNA结合亲和力的影响，聚焦蛋白-DNA互作且采用物理模拟方法，但对象为TP63而非典型TF-DNA体系，深度有限。
abstract: Single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) help to understand the phenotypic variations in humans. Genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified SNPs located in the tumor protein 63 (TP63) locus to be associated with the genetic susceptibility of cancers. However, there is a lack of in-depth characterization of the structural and functional impacts of the SNPs located at the TP63 gene. The current study was designed for the comprehensive characterization of the coding and non-coding SNPs in the human TP63 gene for their functional and structural significance. The functional and structural effects of the SNPs were investigated using a wide variety of computational tools and approaches, including molecular dynamics (MD) simulation. The deleterious impact of eight nonsynonymous SNPs (nsSNPs) affecting protein stability, structure, and functions was measured by using 13 bioinformatics tools. These eight nsSNPs are in highly conserved positions in protein and were predicted to decrease protein stability and have a deleterious impact on the TP63 protein function. Molecular docking analysis showed five nsSNPs to reduce the binding affinity of TP63 protein to DNA with significant results for three SNPs (R319H, G349E, and C347F). Further, MD simulations revealed the possible disruption of TP63 and DNA binding, hampering the essential protein function. PolymiRTS study found five non-coding SNPs in miRNA binding sites, and the GTEx portal recognized five eQTLs SNPs in single tissue of the lung, heart (LV), and cerebral hemisphere (brain). Characterized nsSNPs and non-coding SNPs will help researchers to focus on TP63 gene loci and ascertain their association with certain diseases.
abstract_zh: 单核苷酸多态性（SNPs）有助于理解人类表型变异。全基因组关联研究（GWAS）已识别出位于肿瘤蛋白63（TP63）基因座中的SNPs与癌症的遗传易感性相关。然而，对于TP63基因中SNPs的结构和功能影响，目前缺乏深入的表征。本研究旨在全面表征人类TP63基因中编码区和非编码区SNPs的功能和结构意义。通过多种计算工具和方法，包括分子动力学（MD）模拟，研究了SNPs的功能和结构效应。利用13种生物信息学工具，测量了八个非同义SNPs（nsSNPs）对蛋白质稳定性、结构和功能的有害影响。这八个nsSNPs位于蛋白质中高度保守的位置，预测会降低蛋白质稳定性，并对TP63蛋白功能产生有害影响。分子对接分析显示，五个nsSNPs降低了TP63蛋白与DNA的结合亲和力，其中三个SNPs（R319H、G349E和C347F）的结果显著。进一步，MD模拟揭示了TP63与DNA结合可能被破坏，从而阻碍了关键的蛋白质功能。PolymiRTS研究发现miRNA结合位点中有五个非编码SNPs，而GTEx门户识别出在肺、心脏（左心室）和大脑半球（脑）单一组织中的五个eQTLs SNPs。所表征的nsSNPs和非编码SNPs将有助于研究人员聚焦于TP63基因座，并确定其与特定疾病的关联。
